head: cb4c5fa3
subject: HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 concurrent worker-pool cap
change: serveConcurrentStreams now accepts max_worker_threads. Null preserves the existing lazy growth up to max_streams; a configured value caps the per-connection worker pool and is clamped to 1..max_streams. Summary.workers_spawned reports the actual number of handler threads created, so callers and tests can verify the cap. This gives consumers a way to trade handler concurrency for less thread-scheduling contention on CPU-bound workloads while keeping accepted streams and bodies bounded by the existing owner queues.

http3.command: zig build test-lib -Dtest-filter='HTTP/3 continuous concurrent' --summary all
http3.coverage: The two-stream continuous-serving test runs with max_worker_threads=1, proves both handlers complete through one worker while the owner buffers bodies and responses, and asserts summary.workers_spawned <= 1.

http2.coverage: The four-stream concurrent test runs with max_worker_threads=1, including the oversize-stream sibling case, and asserts summary.workers_spawned <= 1.

notes: The default remains one possible worker per max_streams so existing latency-sensitive streaming behavior is unchanged. The option is a tuning boundary, not a claim that a lower cap is faster for every workload.
